title: Control-room shell frame and J1 board slice
description: Task B of the control-room shell pre-split (architect-d89636d1; honest combined file map was 18-20 vs the caps — split before code exists per the size-governance memories). Objective: the shell FRAME plus the minimal operable J1 slice over the Task-A scaffold. Deliverable, using the verification findings pinned here (do not rediscover): src/shell/ = frame ONLY (nav rail + main outlet + inspector + status strip per spec line 51; the BOARD is a surface, spec §2.2) + provenance drill-down panel consuming the shell-local DEVELOPMENT_ONLY provenance fixture type (spec §3.2 popover shape: event seq+ID, actor/session, lease epoch, timestamp, typed link — no repo-wide provenance type exists; follow the testkit FOUNDATION_FAKE_KIND marker pattern); minimal J1 slices placed in the CANONICAL DOWNSTREAM DIRECTORIES (spec §6.1 lines 499-509: goals form 503; board columns cr.board.column.* with name/phase/chip cards, NO joinstrip/silence-timer/terminated-filter; approval detail with cr.action.approval-decide.approve for plan+acceptance kinds; node inspector chipped facts only, no §10.5 attempt detail; evidence receipt exit-0 + base/head SHAs; doctor = cr.health.status summary only) — the five downstream surface tasks own those dirs and BUILD OVER these slices, never duplicate them (the rejected alternative was src/surfaces/ stubs that become undeletable dead duplicates). ACTION-GATING SEMANTICS (spec-verified, the earlier draft was WRONG): disconnected fixture => ALL cr.action.* DISABLED (not hidden) + banner (spec 524/530, role=status/alert per 687); LAG/STALE fixture => stale display LABELED, commands NOT blocked (spec 614, CR-LAG-001 739); daemon-reason-coded-disabled is a SEPARATE provisional DEVELOPMENT_ONLY fixture channel (NextAllowedCommand carries no reason field; §13-D2 registry unratified — no daemon reason => control ABSENT, never disabled-with-guessed-text, spec 588-590); actions render ONLY from supplied readonly NextAllowedCommand[] (@moe/contracts buildNextAllowedCommands/EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS). Graph tab renders as a NON-MOUNTING placeholder and a test asserts cr.graph.* is NEVER mounted during the J1 flow (spec 509/CR-J1-002 722). Triple encoding comes from the Task-A kernel adapter (describeTruthClass re-export with the absent-class→UNKNOWN mapping); every cr.fact.* has a cr.chip.* descendant (spec 742 bar 3), 24px hit target + aria-label composition + UNKNOWN dashed border (spec 176). Keyboard/a11y for THIS task: jsdom-testable roles/labels/focus-order/keyboard basics via @testing-library (spec 684/687/691 — Enter/p provenance); NO axe dep; WCAG/monochrome/latency + Playwright journeys belong to Accessibility latency hardening and Control-room journey gate. FIXTURE CONTENT TRIPWIRE: no fixture string may contain 'packages/scheduler/src/' or '@moe/scheduler/' or 'scheduler/src/' literals (scheduler package-boundary test scans apps/** .tsx CONTENTS at the root gate) and no fixture module imports a path containing 'foundation/' (testkit foundation-spec scans apps/** .ts import specifiers). Named import { userEvent } (default-import fails tsc under NodeNext — proven). Hard dependency: Task A (Foundation control-room shell, task-fd82678f) — scaffold, kernel adapter, fixtures, and the frontend dependency set must be landed first; block if absent. Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/shell/**, apps/control-room/src/board/**, apps/control-room/src/goals/**, apps/control-room/src/approvals/**, apps/control-room/src/nodes/**, apps/control-room/src/evidence/**, apps/control-room/src/doctor/**, and app-level test files for these slices. Keep total files <=10 (merge tests: one gating+keyboard test, one board/J1 flow test) and every file <=250 lines. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test.
definitionOfDone: The shell frame renders nav/outlet/inspector/status-strip with the Graph tab as a never-mounted placeholder, proven by a test asserting no cr.graph.* mounts during the J1 flow.

The J1 slice is operable end-to-end on fixtures: goals form, board columns with chip cards, approval decide action, node inspector chipped facts, evidence receipt line, doctor status summary — each in its canonical downstream directory.

Action gating matches the spec exactly: disconnected disables all actions with a banner; lag labels stale without blocking; absent daemon reason renders no control; actions derive only from supplied NextAllowedCommand[].
Keyboard reachability, roles/labels, and provenance drill-down (Enter/p) pass jsdom tests; the focused control-room typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Frame-and-slice only: the five downstream surface tasks own the full surfaces and build over the J1 slices in place — do not pre-build their scope and do not create src/surfaces/, src/a11y/, or src/performance/.
Never mutate from the client: no client-derived authority; disabled/absent semantics per spec 524/530/588-590/614; no guessed disabled-reason text.
Fixture strings must never contain scheduler path literals; fixture modules must never import 'foundation/' paths.
Every file <=250 lines; <=10 files total; explicit-pathspec commit only.

Task A shipped none, and NextAllowedCommand (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-affordance.ts:18-28) has NO reason field. SPEC PINS RE-READ AND CORRECTED vs description: (a) nav rail (line 58) is Goals/Approvals/Runs-Leases/Resources/Health/Policy — Graph is NOT a rail item; it is a projection tab in the context bar (line 51). Placeholder goes on the tab. (b) CR-J1-002 bar text is `cr.graph.canvas` never mounted; I assert the stronger `cr.graph.*`. (c) Columns are exactly cr.board.column.{plan|ready|executing|review|accepted} (line 95). (d) Enablement authority = snapshot.mutationsEnabled (daemon-derived in fixture), never client-recomputed: DISCONNECTED+commands -> false (renders disabled), LAGGING+commands -> true (renders enabled, CR-LAG-001).
(e) CRITICAL for the disabled-not-hidden proof: the canonical DISCONNECTED snapshot carries EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS, so it renders ZERO controls and cannot prove "disabled, not hidden". MUTATION_BLOCK_ISOLATION[0] (DISCONNECTED + real commands) is the only fixture that can. Using it.
(f) Spec 3.2 names the provenance popover `cr.chip.provenance`, which collides with convention-control-room-test-id-prefixes ("cr.chip.* counts chips exactly"). Resolution: keep the spec id but render the panel at shell level, never inside a cr.fact.* wrapper, and assert the bar-3 audit per-wrapper so it is immune to the panel.
Toolchain: named `import { userEvent }`; NO jest-dom in the dep set, so no toBeInTheDocument — use toBeTruthy/.disabled/getAttribute.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/shell/gating-keyboard.test.tsx (<=250; NAMED import { userEvent }). The action-gating matrix (spec-exact, all via Task A fixtures): (1) CONNECTED fixture: actions render ONLY from the supplied readonly NextAllowedCommand[] — for each affordance an enabled control with its cr.action.* testid; EMPTY affordances -> ZERO action controls in the DOM (absent, not disabled); (2) DISCONNECTED fixture: banner with role=status/alert (spec 687) AND every cr.action.* control DISABLED (present, not hidden — spec 524); assert the banner and enabled-action states never coexist (spec 530); (3) LAG/STALE fixture: stale display LABELED (visible stale marker testid) while controls stay ENABLED — commands NOT blocked (spec 614 / CR-LAG-001); (4) REASON-CODED-DISABLED provisional channel: only the separate DEVELOPMENT_ONLY fixture channel may render disabled-with-reason; a fixture affordance WITHOUT a daemon reason renders NO control ever disabled-with-guessed-text (spec 588-590); (5) KEYBOARD: every rendered control reachable in DOM order (tab traversal via userEvent), roles/labels present; provenance drill-down opens via Enter and 'p' (spec 691) showing the §3.2 popover fields from the fixture provenance type; focus returns on close. Each assertion targets the spec testid taxonomy (cr.action.*, cr.chip.*, cr.banner.*). Confirm RED.
implementationPlan.note:
src/shell/gating-keyboard.test.tsx written, 242 lines, RED confirmed (Failed to resolve import "./frame.js" — production surface does not exist yet). Named `import { userEvent }` per the proven NodeNext constraint.

12 cases covering the spec-exact matrix. Non-vacuity is guarded everywhere a loop or a fixture lookup could silently test nothing:
- CONNECTED: control count === supplied nextAllowedCommands.length (so an extra client-invented action fails), each enabled, plus an explicit assert that actionTestId(approval.decide) === the spec-pinned "cr.action.approval-decide.approve".
- EMPTY commands (MUTATION_BLOCK_ISOLATION[2], CONNECTED+none): ZERO controls — absent, not disabled.
- DISCONNECTED: uses MUTATION_BLOCK_ISOLATION[0] deliberately, and the test comments why — the canonical DISCONNECTED snapshot carries EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS, so it renders zero controls and literally cannot distinguish "disabled" from "hidden". Only the drop-while-holding-affordances leg proves spec 524. Asserts banner role is status|alert, control count === command count (present), every one disabled.
- Banner/enabled coexistence (spec 530 / CR-J3-001) swept over all 7 snapshots with a bannersSeen counter asserted > 0, so the sweep cannot pass by never meeting a banner.
- LAGGING: statusstrip data-stale=true + lag banner carrying the fixture statusLabel, disconnected banner absent, every control ENABLED (CR-LAG-001).
- No-invented-reason: sweeps every snapshot asserting each DISABLED control has no data-reason-code, no title, no "Unavailable" text, with a disabledSeen counter asserted > 0; plus a source scan of frame.tsx for the literals "Unavailable"/"REASON_CODE", since with no reason field on NextAllowedCommand a hard-coded string is the only way one could reach the DOM.
- Keyboard: real userEvent.tab() traversal collecting focus order and asserting it equals DOM order exactly (not merely "all reachable"), aria-label present on each; landmarks present; zero cr.graph.* mounted.
- Provenance: Enter on a focused chip opens cr.chip.provenance showing all seven §3.2 fields (uses goals[1], a receipt-linked fact whose leaseEpoch is non-null, asserted non-null first so the epoch assertion is real) + cr.timeline.jump; Escape closes AND focus returns to the chip. Separate case for the 'p' shortcut (spec 691). Separate case pins absent-class -> cr.chip.unknown with dashed border and the TRUTH_ABSENT_PROVENANCE aria text.

Asserted reason codes/testids, not bare outcomes, per the new epic rail.

implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: 13/13 in gating-keyboard.test.tsx. frame.tsx 219 lines, provenance-panel.tsx 151, test 247 — all <=250.

frame.tsx: nav rail (6 spec-line-58 items) + context bar with the three projection tabs + main outlet + inspector + status strip. Frame only; no board. GatingContext publishes {actionsEnabled, commands, stale} straight from the supplied snapshot — actionsEnabled IS affordance.mutationsEnabled, never recomputed client-side; the context default is fail-closed (actionsEnabled false, EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS) so a surface rendered outside a frame gets zero authority. ActionButton renders one control per supplied NextAllowedCommand and has NO onClick and no envelope construction — render-only. Graph tab selects a placeholder carrying testid cr.shell.graphplaceholder, deliberately NOT a cr.graph.* id.
provenance-panel.tsx: ProvenanceProvider captures document.activeElement BEFORE the panel mounts and restores it on close (keyboard trap avoidance); ProvenancePanel is role=dialog, self-focusing, Escape-dismissable, renders all seven §3.2 fields + cr.timeline.jump. FactWithProvenance delegates the claim to the kernel's Fact (truth logic never reimplemented) and adds only the affordance: kernel onProvenance for click/Enter, plus a bubbled 'p' keydown. Panel renders at shell level, never inside a cr.fact.* wrapper.

MUTATION RED-CHECKS (backup out of tree, restore verified by git hash-object -> identical 1234b79b both sides):
- disabled={!actionsEnabled} -> disabled={false}: 3 failed / 10 passed. Disconnected-disables and coexistence both catch it.
- disconnected banner removed: 2 failed / 11 passed — and critically one of those is the coexistence sweep failing on bannersSeen === 0, proving that guard stops the sweep passing vacuously.
- data-stale forced "false": 1 failed / 12 passed.
All three go red; none was a test that only asserts an outcome.

TOOLCHAIN GOTCHA FOUND (new, worth a memory): @vitejs/plugin-react rewrites import.meta.url inside .tsx to an http://localhost:3000/ URL, so the scaffold's readOwnSource(fileURLToPath(new URL(f, import.meta.url))) pattern throws "TypeError: The URL must be of scheme file" when copied into a nested .tsx test. Source scans must resolve from process.cwd() (the Vitest root) instead. I added a positive marker assert (source contains "export function ShellFrame") so the two not.toContain checks cannot pass by reading an empty or wrong file — a silent-empty read would otherwise make this test permanently, invisibly green.
